blindComparison: A stranger picks the reference every time, and the reason is not detail — it is that in KAGEROU nothing on the ground is attached to anything above it. In Tsushima's golden-hour approach or Sekiro's Ashina Outskirts at dusk, the low sun writes the composition on the floor: every post, lantern and eave throws a long raking shadow, and those shadows are what tell you the ground is a surface and the objects are standing on it. In phone-torii-r8 the left torii post is measurably lit from the left (post RGB 173,51,27 on the sunward face vs 60,7,3 on the shadow face at the same height) and the flagstone strip on its shadow side (899,1106 128x41, luma p50 40.5) is BRIGHTER than open flagstone 200 px away (1114,1106, p50 31.7). A six-metre post at a low sun angle and there is not one pixel of shadow beside it. The eye reads that instantly as objects pasted onto a photograph of a floor. Second reason: two of the five frames hand the viewer a vast empty plain — phone-valley-r8's floor is 45% of the frame at meanRGB 166,98,50 with no grass, no rock and no undergrowth, only one repeated pale ellipse blob tiled a few hundred times. The reference never shows you an empty field; it shows you grass moving in a wind.
acrossTheSet: From the contact sheet: composition is genuinely improving — phone-torii-r8 and phone-sun-r8 have real foreground/mid/background staging and a readable torii silhouette, and phone-sun-r8's contre-jour is the best single image this project has produced. But the five frames do not read as one place at one hour. Whole-frame means: hero 90.4/81.3/77.3 (sat 0.329), wide 88.3/86.8/89.2 (sat 0.213), torii 93.6/87.9/87.5 (sat 0.378), valley 111.0/75.9/47.8 (sat 0.625), sun 138.8/112.6/92.0 (sat 0.448). wide has R-B = -0.9 — literally no warm bias at all, an overcast-dusk image — while valley sits at R-B = +63 in blazing orange. Same build, same clock, two different times of day.

findings.problem: No object in any of the four daylight framings casts a shadow onto the ground, at any distance, despite an unambiguous low key light. Measured in phone-torii-r8: the torii's sunward post face is 173,51,27 and its shade face 60,7,3 (boxes 848,527 46x176 and 1557,527 46x176), so the key is confidently from frame-left; yet flagstone immediately on the shadow side of the left post (899,1106 128x41) reads luma p50 40.5 while open flagstone 215 px further right at the same depth (1114,1106 128x41) reads p50 31.7 — the shadow side is brighter than the open ground. Same on the right post: 1620,1082 (p50 12.6) vs open ground 1823,1082 (p50 15.8), a 3-unit difference in the wrong direction. In phone-wide-r8 the entire shrine complex — two shrine halls, three torii, ~20 stone lanterns, four fence runs, a bridge — stands on the plain between y=600 and y=900 and not one of them darkens the ground beneath or beside it; the plain reads a flat 37,35,35 on the left (253,725 380x117) and 42,40,42 on the right (1899,725), i.e. uniform ambient with no directional occlusion anywhere. In phone-hero-r8 the two stone lanterns at x~1560 and x~1830 sit on the plaza with no cast shadow and no contact darkening at their plinths.
findings.why: This is the single thing that separates a shipped console frame from a viewport screenshot. Golden hour in Tsushima is composed *by* the shadows — long raking bars across the ground that describe the terrain's undulation and anchor every prop to it. Without them the ground is an unlit backdrop and every object reads as a cutout floated in front of it, no matter how good the mesh is. Every other improvement in this frame is invisible until this is fixed.
findings.fix: Every prop in the shrine complex must cast a directional shadow at this sun elevation. Target, verifiable against a re-shoot of phone-torii-r8: the left torii post (screen x~890, base at y~1130) throws a shadow bar at least 250 px long running to frame-right and slightly toward camera, with a hard contact at the plinth (the first ~15 px of the bar should read luma p50 below 15 against surrounding flagstone at p50 ~32, i.e. a factor-2 drop) softening by ~40% at the far end. In phone-wide-r8 the ~20 stone lanterns between x=600 and x=1400 must each read as a visible dark streak on the plain; the current left/right plain patches (253,725 and 1899,725) differ by only 5 luma units — after the fix the histogram of a 400x120 box containing three lantern bases must show a bimodal split of at least 25 luma units between shadowed and unshadowed flagstone. Verify by measuring the same two boxes before and after; byte-identical numbers mean the branch you edited is not what draws those pixels.
findings.hypothesis: UNVERIFIED — do not act on this before disproving it: the shadow casters may be receiving shadows but the ground receiver may be excluded, or the cascade covering the 0-40 m band may be resolving to a depth range that never contains the ground plane. Prove or disprove by ablation (force the ground to render shadow-map depth as albedo) before changing any light parameter.

findings.problem: Every high-contrast silhouette edge in the set is outlined in a 1-2 px band of saturated green on one side and magenta on the other. This is not subtle at native resolution: on the shrine roofline against the sky at frame centre — pixel (1244,469) is RGB 54,130,50, (1250,480) is 95,142,94, (1252,484) is 85,144,86, a continuous green line running the length of the eave — and the underside of the same edge carries magenta. The roof tile battens above it (823,491 to 975,561) alternate white / green / magenta on every rib, turning a wood-and-tile roof into colour noise. It occurs at the optical centre of the frame (x=1244 of 2532 is 0.49) with the same magnitude as at the frame edge (2274,491 = 63,108,67), so it is not a radial falloff. It also lands on the lantern paper panels in phone-wide-r8 (1201,608 = 112,163,80; 1180,666 = 134,192,99), making lit lanterns read as green-striped rather than amber.
findings.why: Coloured fringing on every edge is the visual signature of a broken pipeline, not a photographic lens. A viewer does not name it, but it makes all fine architectural detail — tile ribs, railing balusters, shoji mullions, rope fibre — read as buzzing chromatic noise instead of material. It is also the reason the frames look 'crunchy' rather than filmic: the same edges are hard-aliased with no antialiasing under the fringe, so you get a stair-stepped silhouette wearing a green outline.
findings.fix: The green/magenta channel separation must be zero at the optical centre and at most sub-pixel anywhere in frame. Verifiable target on a re-shoot of phone-hero-r8: in box 1215,468 152x35 (shrine eave against sky, frame centre) there must be zero pixels satisfying G>90 AND G-R>40 AND G-B>40 — there are currently 55 in that region. Repeat for box 2229,491 152x35 (frame edge), currently 51. Separately, that same eave silhouette is a hard un-antialiased staircase; the edge should resolve with sub-pixel coverage so a 6x zoom of 1215,468 shows intermediate values between roof and sky rather than a binary step.
findings.hypothesis: UNVERIFIED: could be a chromatic-aberration pass with a non-zero constant term rather than a radius-scaled one, or a sharpen/upsample kernel running per-channel at a channel offset. Measure the per-channel edge position on a single high-contrast vertical edge before touching either.

findings.problem: A horizontal band of detached magenta/crimson rectangular dashes floats in the clear sky above the bamboo canopy line, unconnected to any geometry. In phone-valley-r8, band y=0..152, x=127..1520: 513 pixels satisfy R>110 AND R-G>55 AND B>=G, e.g. (166,120) = RGB 164,45,91, (214,141) = 179,65,89, (226,117) = 155,69,96, (307,122) = 168,77,97. At 6x these are clearly 4-10 px horizontal dashes sitting in empty sky, some 60+ px above the nearest canopy silhouette and well to the left of any bamboo at all. The same defect appears in phone-sun-r8 across the whole horizon strip (279 such pixels in y=679..749, x=127..1646: (136,693) = 131,72,97; (735,713) = 154,90,113; (1013,735) = 232,128,151) as an evenly spaced dotted line of maroon dashes above the treeline, and again in phone-wide-r8 along the bamboo band at y~360-400.
findings.why: It reads as dirt on the lens or dead pixels on the display. Nothing else in the frame matters once a viewer notices garbage floating in the sky — it is the one artefact that says 'this is broken software' rather than 'this is a place'. It sits on the horizon line, exactly where the eye rests.
findings.fix: Zero pixels above the canopy silhouette may be magenta/crimson. Verifiable target on a re-shoot: in phone-valley-r8 region x,y,w,h = 0.05,0.0,0.55,0.13 the count of pixels satisfying R>110 AND R-G>55 AND B>=G must be 0 (currently 513); in phone-sun-r8 region 0.05,0.58,0.60,0.06 it must be 0 (currently 279). Also address what sits underneath them: in phone-valley-r8 the mid-distance bamboo between x=850 and x=1400, y=250..350 is a set of bare vertical poles with no leaf mass at their tops — culms that terminate in nothing, which is why the canopy silhouette is a ragged fringe rather than a mass.
findings.hypothesis: UNVERIFIED: the colour is close to the sakura petal tint, so these may be blossom or leaf cards whose alpha test is passing on texels that should be transparent, or a card LOD whose billboard degenerates to a horizontal sliver at distance. Do not assume; sample one dash's screen position across two frames to see whether it is world-anchored before changing any shader.

findings.problem: The ground in the two landscape framings is a bare, featureless plain covering roughly half the image with nothing growing on it. In phone-valley-r8 the floor (253,410 1139x293) is meanRGB 166,98,50, saturation 0.711, detail 7.6 — a single-hue orange mud field whose only feature is one pale elliptical blob repeated in a regular scatter several hundred times at identical size and orientation across the whole basin; the only vegetation is a handful of single-pixel-wide yellow stems in the lower third. Bamboo culms enter this dirt with no root clutter, no undergrowth and no contact darkening. In phone-wide-r8 the plain from y=600 to y=1170 is uniform grey speckle (253,725 = 37,35,35; 1899,725 = 42,40,42, both detail <5) with no paths, no terrain undulation, no grass, no rock, and props standing on it in isolation.
findings.why: This is the 'level editor with props dropped in' failure from the brief, at full scale. A Tsushima field at this hour is deep grass in motion — the wind field is the subject and the ground is never visible as bare substrate. Here half the frame is an untouched noise texture, which also destroys the mid-ground: phone-wide-r8 has a foreground of lanterns and a background of mountains with a grey void in between. The repeated identical blob is worse than no detail, because it announces the tiling.
findings.fix: The valley basin and the shrine plain must carry ground cover and surface variety. Verifiable targets on a re-shoot: (a) phone-valley-r8 box 0.10,0.35,0.45,0.25 must reach detail > 16 (currently 7.57) and saturation below 0.55 (currently 0.711) — i.e. real high-frequency ground cover with more than one hue in it, not a single orange wash; (b) the repeated pale ellipse must not be identifiable as one recurring shape — no single 40x20 px motif may appear more than ~5 times in a 1139x293 crop; (c) phone-wide-r8 box 0.10,0.62,0.15x0.10 and 0.75,0.62,0.15x0.10 must stop being within 5 luma units of each other (currently p50 33.4 vs 38.6) — the plain needs readable undulation, a worn path between the torii and the shrine, and scattered rock/grass so the mid-ground has structure. Measure the same boxes before and after; identical numbers mean you edited a branch that does not draw this ground.

findings.problem: The distant range on the right (x=1290..2280, y=200..400) is a row of literal flat-shaded isoceles triangles: perfectly straight ridgelines, smooth untextured faces, one uniform lavender value. Box 1760,287 127x59 reads detail 1.28 and lumaSpread 24.4 — for comparison the adjacent empty sky at 1671,187 152x47 reads detail 0.69. The mountains are within half a luma unit of the sky they sit against (p50 154.5 vs 155.5) and carry almost no more surface variation than it. The far right ridge at 2102,316 is worse: detail 1.08. The nearer massif at 380,117 at least reaches detail 3.99, but that is still a flat wash at 1.8 km. There is also no aerial-perspective separation between the 900 m massif and the 1.8 km peaks — they read at the same value and same saturation.
findings.why: The horizon is the second thing a viewer looks at after the subject, and Tsushima sells its scale entirely on layered ridgelines that get bluer, softer and more atmospheric with each layer. A row of flat cones with mathematically straight edges reads as placeholder geometry — it is the one element in the set that looks unfinished rather than stylised.
findings.fix: The distant range needs broken ridgelines and surface variation. Verifiable target on a re-shoot of phone-wide-r8: box 0.695,0.245,0.05,0.05 must reach detail > 4.0 (currently 1.28) with lumaSpread > 45 (currently 24.4) — rock faces, gullies, a snowline that follows terrain rather than a clean geometric cut. The silhouette must not contain a straight segment longer than ~60 px. Separately, aerial perspective must separate the layers: box 0.83,0.27 (far ridge) should sit at least 12 luma units closer to the sky value and at least 0.03 lower in saturation than box 0.15,0.10 (near massif); currently they are 150.7 vs 133.5 with saturations 0.057 and 0.081, which is the right sign but far too weak to read.
findings.hypothesis: UNVERIFIED: the far peaks may be a separate low-cost backdrop mesh rather than the heightfield, in which case this belongs partly to whoever generates that mesh. Confirm which system draws x=1290..2280,y=200..400 before editing.

findings.shot: phone-wide-r8 (against the rest of the set)
findings.problem: phone-wide-r8 is a different time of day from the other four frames. Whole-frame meanRGB is 88.3,86.8,89.2 with saturation 0.213 — R minus B is -0.9, i.e. a cold neutral, no warm key at all. The other frames at the same clock: hero 90.4,81.3,77.3 (R-B +13.1), torii 93.6,87.9,87.5 (+6.1), sun 138.8,112.6,92.0 (+46.8), valley 111.0,75.9,47.8 (+63.2). Side by side on the contact sheet, wide reads as an overcast blue hour while valley reads as a blazing sunset. Nothing in wide carries a warm sunward face — the shrine roofs, the vermilion torii and the plain are all in the same cold band.
findings.why: A shipped title's marketing set is colour-graded as one thing; five frames of one location at one hour must share a key temperature or the set reads as screenshots from different builds. It also means wide — the establishing shot, the one that has to sell the world — is the least attractive image in the set.
findings.fix: At this sun elevation, phone-wide-r8 must carry the same warm key as phone-torii-r8. Verifiable target on a re-shoot: whole-frame mean R minus mean B must be at least +6 (currently -0.9), and a sunward-facing surface must exist in the frame that reads meanRGB with R at least 40 above B — currently no such region exists in wide. The cool side must remain cool: the plain in shadow should keep B >= R so the frame carries a warm/cool split rather than a uniform warm wash.
findings.hypothesis: UNVERIFIED: this framing may be looking away from the sun so that everything visible is sky-lit, in which case the fault is that the sky probe is overwhelming the key rather than that the key is missing. Ablate the sky contribution in this camera before touching sun colour.

findings.problem: The sakura reads as a pink cauliflower, not a tree. In phone-hero-r8 (crop 127,23 810x468) the canopy is a mass of overlapping semi-transparent blossom cards with visible rectangular card boundaries and pale square alpha patches, no branch armature connecting it to a trunk, and dozens of hard straight dark spikes radiating out of the blossom mass at every angle — unlit twig geometry punching through the cards, which at a glance reads as pine needles stuck into a pink cloud. The silhouette is a single convex blob with one straggling lump hanging below it. In phone-wide-r8 the same tree at x=750..900, y=370..460 is a solid pink puff with no structure at all.
findings.why: The cherry tree is the signature object of this setting and it is the least convincing mesh in the frame. Tsushima's trees read at thumbnail size as a branch structure carrying clumps — you can see where the limbs go. Here the silhouette carries no information, and at native resolution the card edges and needle spikes are plainly visible artefacts rather than blossom.
findings.fix: The canopy must read as clumps hung on visible branches. Verifiable on a re-shoot of phone-hero-r8 region 0.05,0.02,0.32,0.40: the silhouette against the sky must be concave in at least three places (gaps you can see sky through, between clumps) rather than one convex blob, and the dark straight twig spikes currently projecting beyond the blossom outline must terminate inside the blossom mass, not outside it. Blossom card edges must not be resolvable as straight-line rectangle boundaries at native resolution.

findings.problem: The ground carries dark elliptical blobs that are not attached to anything. In phone-sun-r8 (crop 709,913 886x257) there are soft dark ovals at crop-relative (60,80), (200,130), (330,100) and (700,190) sitting on open sand with no object above them, while the torii post at crop x=380..490 — with the sun directly behind it — casts nothing at all. In phone-hero-r8 the plaza at crop 1063,585 has a large soft dark blob around crop (230,500) to (500,470), again floating free of any caster. They read as oil puddles or wet patches, not as shadow.
findings.why: Free-floating dark ovals on the ground are worse than no shadows at all: they set the viewer's expectation that shadows exist, then break it, so the eye immediately notices that the actual objects have none. It is the specific reading that makes a frame look like a debug view.
findings.fix: No ground darkening may appear where there is no object above it. Verifiable on a re-shoot of phone-sun-r8: in box 0.28,0.78,0.35,0.22, every region reading more than 20 luma units below the local sand mean must lie directly beneath a visible caster. If these are intended as ambient-occlusion or blob shadows they must be anchored to and scaled by their caster, and they must vanish once real cast shadows land (see the Lighting.js blocker) so the two do not double up.
findings.hypothesis: UNVERIFIED: these could equally be a terrain splat/wetness layer rather than a decal system. Determine which pass writes those pixels before editing anything in Effects.js, and if it is terrain, hand this finding to src/world/Terrain.js.

findings.problem: The shimenawa rope reads as a machine-extruded corrugated pipe. In phone-torii-r8 (x=700..1200, y=410..500) the fibre pattern is a perfectly regular chevron ribbing at constant pitch along the entire span, with no variation in twist, no loose fibres, no shide paper streamers, and a silhouette that is a clean mathematical catenary with no sag asymmetry. Same read in phone-sun-r8 in silhouette.
findings.why: It is the hero prop hanging at eye level in the centre of two of five frames, and it currently says 'procedural geometry' rather than 'rice straw'. Sekiro's ropes are lumpy, asymmetric, and shed fibre.
findings.fix: Break the regularity: vary the twist pitch and radius along the span so no two 100 px stretches look identical, add stray fibre silhouette breaking the outline, and hang shide (zigzag paper streamers) from it. Verifiable: in phone-torii-r8 box 0.28,0.36,0.20,0.06 the horizontal autocorrelation of the rib pattern must no longer show a single dominant constant period.

findings.problem: The tall standing banners are flat untextured dark quads. In phone-torii-r8 the banner at x=1722..2076, y=491..842 is a single near-uniform dark rectangle with faint noise, no lettering, no hem, no fold, no wind curl, and no lit face despite a clear key light from frame-left; it also leans at an angle that intersects the lantern roof in front of it. Two more of the same at x=540..600 and in phone-sun-r8 at x=1000..1080.
findings.why: Nobori banners are one of the strongest silhouette and colour opportunities in this setting — vertical vermilion strips with black kanji that catch and translucently glow with a low sun. As flat black rectangles they read as missing textures.
findings.fix: Give the banners a lit face (their sunward side should read at least 60 luma units above their shade side at this key angle), translucency so the low sun shows through the cloth, kanji, a stitched hem, and a slow wind curl driven by the single wind field. Fix the placement so no banner intersects the lantern roof in front of it.
